properties.description: Welcome Home to First Hill's Terry Terrace #206, historic old world charm  &  one of the best kept secrets in Seattle! Like an unassuming geode, this condo keeps its sparkle a secret—until you step inside. A smart  floor plan, 9 windows of light combined w/ high ceilings, crown molding, &  picture rails, this home spans the full length of the building. 2 bdms  &  a full bath anchor one end of the condo, while the living, dining, &  kitchen spaces stretch out on the other. The entryway is the ideal gallery space to showcase your favorite art. Freshly painted and  move-in ready. EXCELLENT INVESTOR OPPORTUNITY- LOW HOA DUES, SHORT TERM (3 month) RENTAL, NO RENTAL CAP! This unique community is perched on top of the historic Old Johnson's Plumbing Building and perfectly represents Seattle's rich history and modernized future. Your 1 bed, 1 bath unit is move-in ready with high-end finishes and a spacious and efficient layout. There are two large closets for storage, full-sized washer/dryer, and an oversized bathroom vanity. Your living room boasts large windows, space for hosting, and a nook perfect for a desk. Penthouse studio with stunning Puget Sound and city views! This charming top-floor unit offers an ideal in-city retreat with exposed brick, warm wood floors, and a Murphy bed for flexible living and sleeping space. Enjoy access to a secure community garden and inviting outdoor patio area—perfect for relaxing or entertaining. Additional highlights include a private storage unit, no rental cap, pet-friendly community, and no special assessments. With a Walk Score of 97, you’re ready for the best of Seattle’s dining, shopping, entertainment, transit, and nightlife. Centrally located and full of character, this is city living at its best!

Experience the best of Pioneer Square living from this west-facing home at the iconic Gridiron. A steel and glass modern building on top of a century old brick landmark. The penthouse at 1223 Spring Street is an extraordinary piece of Seattle history and an architectural landmark. Designed in 1929 by prominent Seattle architect Earl Wilson Morrison, the building was conceived to bring the elegance and sophistication of New York’s Park Avenue apartment living to the Pacific Northwest. Sitting atop this Art Deco styled concrete and stone building, the penthouse has been thoughtfully renovated while preserving its defining architectural character, the style is sophisticated, distinctive, and entirely unlike anything else in Seattle.
